newsitem.title: USA: Frederick sees higher gross margins in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Frederick sees higher gross margins in Q3.

text.p: Frederick Brewing Co said Monday it expected lower packaging costs and higher gross margins in the third quarter, despite reporting a $907,000 loss, or $0.45 a share, in the second quarter.
The company said it "expects packaging costs to fall and gross margins to increase in the third quarter with the new bottling line operating at peak efficiency and additional efficiencies".
It added it would improve margins further by increased sales, reducing per barrel cost of production, and by expanded distribution.
The mirco-brewer's loss widened to $907,000, or $0.45 a share, in the quarter ended June 30, compared with a net loss of $336,000, or $0.16 a share, the year before.

Frederick attributed the loss to to higher fixed costs associated with owning and operating the new brewery for the first full quarter; high packaging costs because of delays in bringing the new automated packaging equipment on-line; increasing the company's sales force; additional advertising; and increases in interest payments.
"However, the turn to profitability has now begun with strong growth, an expanding distribution network and lower operating costs," said chief executive Kevin Brannon in a statement.
The brewer's quarterly sales almost doubled to $875,00 from $440,000 last year. Year to date sales rose 30 percent to $1.14 million from $875,000 last year.
Frederick brews Blue Ridge Beers and Hempen Ales. The company's stock traded at 2-1/2 Monday afternoon, up 1/8, but close to its 52-week low of 2-1/8.
